svg.title: An agent opened anywhere versus an agent opened in your brain
svg.desc: Two fictional terminal sessions ask whether the new website can launch. Opened anywhere, the agent has no access to Jira, GitHub or Google Cloud and asks you to paste them. Opened in a brain, it reads project:new-website, finds four records from four tools and answers: not yet, the pull request is merged and the preview is healthy, but Jira still blocks launch on accessibility review, citing each record, then notes the launch hold in projects/new-website.md for the next session.
svg.text: Agent opened anywhere
$ cd ~/projects && claude
> Can the new website launch?
● I have no access to your Jira, GitHub
or Google Cloud. Can you paste the
launch review, the pull request and
the deployment status?
✗ Starts blank: you paste the context
✗ Queries the same APIs every session
✗ Forgets its conclusion when it ends
Agent opened in your brain
$ cd ~/brain && claude
> Can the new website launch?
● bf read project:new-website
4 records: workspace, jira, github, gcloud
● Not yet. The pull request is merged and
the preview is healthy, but Jira still
blocks launch on accessibility review.
Evidence: jira:review, github:implementation,
gcloud:deployment
● Noted the launch hold in projects/new-website.md
✓ Starts from your projects and evidence
✓ Cites the record behind each claim
✓ Writes the outcome back for next time
